questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The culture, the great academics, and opportunities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The people in China are not that great at speaking English, but you come a long way knowing a little Chinese.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Okay. In the beginning it can be difficult, but as soon as you receive your acceptance letter, the rest will follow fairly easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Upon arrival, people there are friendly helping you e.g. Finding your way.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Will highly recommend taking part in campus tours and other social activities, in the beginning of the semester.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I lived in the "Global Village" right next to campus which is a great place to live. Here there is both single apartments and shared apartments, but with individual rooms.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There are very small kitchens on each floor (not really suitable for cooking), but I will recommend just eating at uni canteens as it will be cheaper anyways.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
The staff working there are super nice and also very helpful.
There are many nice facilities in the Global Village that you can you like gym, table tennis, badminton, swimming, bowling and much more. These are nice to use :)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
If I could give a tip to future students going there, I will recommend choosing the option to stay with a flat-mate as you still have your own room but share a bathroom and common-room. 

it is a good way to get a friend you will become close with and share some of your experiences with :)

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A good tip is signing up for multiple courses than those you need, to make sure you get the courses you want, and dropping the others afterwards. If you only sign up to the minimum of what you need, you might not get all of them, resulting in you choosing courses you are not that interested in.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Finding the right courses can be challenging, as not all courses in their online overview are available for both semesters.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not sure.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Somewhat successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A good tip is signing up for multiple courses than those you need. This way you will increase the probability that you'll get the courses you want, and the you can just drop the others courses afterwards. If you only sign up to the minimum of what you need, you might not get all of them, resulting in you choosing courses you are not that interested in.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The coursework really depends from course to course. I will recommend you trying to limit the amount of courses you take, to 5 or 6, as you will still have free time then.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The course levels are similar to those in Copenhagen, but I spent more time on school in Peking University.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
It is a bit more traditional, where the tone between teachers and student are a bit more formal.
The style of teaching is also more chalk and blackboard than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Computer Programming in Financial Engineering, Corporate Finance, Distinguished Economists Lectures, Development Economics Behavioral Economics, China's Education and its Cultural Foundation

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I will highly recommend China's Education and its Cultural Foundation to better understand China, and it is a super easy course with no homework and easy exam (just a term paper). 
Also Computer Programming in Financial Engineering is a really good and technical course for quantitative finance.
Behavioral Economics is also quite easy.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Most things are much cheaper than in Denmark, which is nice. The only thing we found that was a little expensive was go-karting.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are hundreds of student clubs.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Pretty much all you can think of.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join of the clubs and befriend some some of the Chinese people there as well. This is a great way to get to know some of the local people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go travel to different parts of China!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try to also understand Chinese culture and their viewpoints. and listen to them.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not that many. If you are open minded it is not a big challenge.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Most Chinese people are very nice when you get to know them, so try your best to do so.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Definitely go!
Try and spend time both with other exchange students and local students. 
Go and travel in other parts of China.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are also a lot of fantastic events hosted on uni, that are very valuable. E.g. Speaks from Oxford chancellor, LSE president and former Director-General of World Trade Organisation (WTO).

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know so many great people and getting to understand China and it culture more deeply.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language barrier in general can be challenging, but again you come a long way with knowing a little Chinese.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
